title: Procedural Validation of Range Invariants
pattern: A function signature accepts a wide primitive type (like i32) and relies on runtime procedural checks or panic assertions to enforce a sub-range invariant (e.g., 1..1000).
why_bad: The type signature 'lies' by claiming to accept any i32. Callers must consult documentation or source code to know the valid range, leading to unexpected runtime panics.
detection: A function accepts a primitive type and immediately executes standard range-checking assertions (e.g., `assert!(x > 0)`) without using a constrained type.
counterexample: A function accepts a pre-validated custom type like `UnitQuantity` which statically guarantees the range invariant.
fix: Create a smart constructor and a private-wrapped type: `struct UnitQuantity(i32);` that can only be created via a validating function.
source: Scott Wlaschin, Domain Modeling Made Functional, p. 201-203 & 536 [201, 536-537].
